issue: ताड़ना: the word's sense is disputed (to beat; to scold or correct; to look after). Gita Press renders it शिक्षा / 'instructions'.
our reading: ताड़ना (कड़ी सीख) / 'stern correction', following our word meaning (discipline, correction)
alternatives: शिक्षा / instruction (Gita Press)
दण्ड, मार / punishment, beating (the literal modern sense)
देखरेख / care, watching over (some commentators)
decided: owner, 2026-10-19: शिक्षा / instruction, with respectful words for the people named (style.md §2)

issue: बिचित्र मनि कृत: do the many-coloured gems adorn the golden wall, or are the mansions made of them?
our reading: the mansions are made of gems (the phrase stands before सुंदरायतना)
alternatives: the golden wall is inlaid with gems (Gita Press)
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: B: the golden wall is set with gems

issue: word meaning, not the verse meaning: library/glossary/awa.json gives जाहू only as 'go' (जाना, imperative). Here (जाहू = whom) and in bal.331.cau4 (सहस मुख जाहू = whose) it is a relative pronoun.
our reading: the meaning reads it as 'whom'; the dictionary entry needs a per-passage sense
alternatives: add the relative sense to the Mānas's own glossary for these two verses
decided: owner asked which lines (sundar.44.cau1, bal.331.cau4); the entry will give both senses: go; whom, whose

review: Disagree with leaving the speaker out. The style rule ('speech simply continues') covers the same speaker going on. Here the speaker changes, and without a tag the line is misattributed to Hanumān. Jāmbavān is plainly implied, not added (compare sundar.2.cau6, where the writer did add one).
reviewer_fix: Open with जाम्बवान्‌जीने कहा — / Jāmbavān said: (see the hi/en fixes above).
decided: applied in review: Jāmbavān named as speaker (style.md §3)

review: Partly disagree with the doubt as written. MW gives नरहरि only as 'Viṣṇu as man-lion' (= Narasiṃha). 'The Lord in human form' is Gita Press's reading, not the dictionary sense. Both readings have support, so the owner should decide knowing that the dictionary favours Narasiṃha. The word sheet entry ('नरसिंह / नररूप हरि') shows both.
reviewer_fix: {"id": "sundar.4.cau1", "issue": "नरहरी: MW gives only 'Viṣṇu as man-lion' (Narasiṃha); 'the Lord in human form' is the commentators' (Gita Press) reading.", "our reading": "नररूप भगवान् / the Lord in human form", "alternatives": ["Narasiṃha, the man-lion (dictionary sense)"]}

issue: हरिं: proper name Hari, or 'the remover (of sins)'. Gita Press renders it 'समस्त पापोंको हरनेवाले'.
our reading: Hari (the name), as in the word meaning: मायासे मनुष्य बने हुए हरि / Hari who appears as a man through māyā.
alternatives: remover of all sins (Gita Press)
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: हरिं: the name Hari (owner leaned to the name; Apte gives हरि first as a name of Viṣṇu, and मायामनुष्यं must qualify a noun) · सुरगुरुं: teacher of the gods

issue: सुरगुरुं: 'teacher of the gods' (word meaning) or 'greatest among the gods' (Gita Press: देवताओंमें सबसे बड़े).
our reading: teacher of the gods / देवताओंके गुरु
alternatives: greatest of the gods
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: हरिं: the name Hari (owner leaned to the name; Apte gives हरि first as a name of Viṣṇu, and मायामनुष्यं must qualify a noun) · सुरगुरुं: teacher of the gods

issue: ALREADY WRITTEN meaning reads 'बिचित्र मनि कृत' with the mansions (mansions made of varied gems); Gita Press reads it with the rampart (a golden rampart inlaid with varied gems). Kept as written.
our reading: a wall of gold, and within it many fine mansions made of gems of every colour
alternatives: a golden rampart studded with gems of many kinds, with many fine mansions inside
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: B: the golden wall is set with gems

issue: नरहरी: the Lord in human form (Rāma), or Narasiṃha.
our reading: नररूप भगवान् / the Lord in human form
alternatives: Narasiṃha, the man-lion

issue: Where Laṅkinī's speech ends: the second half-line (गरल सुधा … सितलाई) runs into 5.cau2, which addresses Garuḍa, so it may be the narrator (Kākabhuśuṇḍi) speaking rather than Laṅkinī. Our meaning runs it on without a speaker, and the address हे गरुड़जी in 5.cau2 shows the narrator.
our reading: no speaker change written; the list runs on into 5.cau2
alternatives: mark the second half-line as the narrator's words to Garuḍa

issue: The verse does not name the speaker; context makes it Jāmbavān's reply to Hanumān (Gita Press inserts [जाम्बवान्‌ने कहा—]). Per the style sheet no speaker is added, so the reader has only हे तात to go on.
our reading: speech given without a speaker tag
alternatives: open with जाम्बवान्‌जीने कहा — / Jāmbavān said: as plainly implied
decided: applied in review: Jāmbavān named as speaker (style.md §3)

issue: जनि करहि निदाना: निदान may mean 'end/limit', 'cause' or 'finally'; the half-line is read in different ways.
our reading: Do not drive my suffering to its last extreme (मेरी पीड़ाको चरम सीमातक मत पहुँचाओ), i.e. do not prolong it to the utmost; give fire instead.
alternatives: Do not delay / do not hold back (just give the fire).
Do not become the cause of further pain.
Give fire at last (निदान = finally), do not refuse.
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: A (owner unsure; kept)

issue: गएँ दिन चारी: literally 'after four days'; often taken idiomatically as 'in a few days'.
our reading: when four days have passed (literal).
alternatives: in a few days' time
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: B: in a few days

issue: हैं सुत कपि सब तुम्हहि समाना: Sītā's line can be read as a statement (all the monkeys are like you, i.e. small), a supposition (they must be like you) or a question (are all the monkeys like you?).
our reading: Statement: सब वानर तो तुम्हारे ही जैसे हैं / the monkeys are all like you; her doubt follows in 16.cau4.
alternatives: Supposition: सब वानर तुम्हारे ही समान होंगे (Gita Press)
Question: क्या सभी वानर तुम्हारे जैसे हैं?

issue: प्रभु कारज लगि कपिहिं बँधावा: the causative बँधावा with object कपिहिं leaves the agent unstated: Hanumān let himself be bound, or (the Lord) had the monkey bound for his work.
our reading: Hanumān let himself be bound for the Lord's work (supported by his decision in 19.do19 to honour the Brahmā weapon).
alternatives: The Lord caused the monkey to be bound for the sake of his own work

issue: जाइ रही पाई बिनु पाई: commentators construe the half-line differently.
our reading: Wealth and power slip away even while they seem to stay; having them is as good as not having them.
alternatives: What has been gained goes away, and what remains is as though never gained.
Once gone it stays gone; gained, it is as if not gained.
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: A (owner unsure; kept)

issue: मधु फल: 'sweet fruit' (मधुर फल) or 'honey and fruit'.
our reading: sweet fruit / मीठे फल
alternatives: honey and fruit / मधु और फल (Gita Press gives this as an alternative)

issue: लोचन निज पद जंत्रित: whose feet are the eyes fixed on? निज normally refers back to the subject (Sītā), i.e. her eyes cast down on her own feet.
our reading: her eyes fixed on her own feet (downcast) are the lock
alternatives: her eyes fixed on your (the Lord's) feet, which she holds in mind, are the lock

review: Disagree with the writer's reading 'helpers': the feminine singular बनी agrees with सहाई as सहायता / संयोग, so the grammar favours the 'situation / combination' reading. Keep the doubt on file, but our reading should be the situation one.
reviewer_fix: {"id": "sundar.38.cau1", "issue": "सोइ रावन कहुँ बनी सहाई: सहाई could be read as 'helpers' (the flattering ministers) or as 'help, combination of circumstances'; the feminine singular बनी agrees with the noun सहाई = सहायता.", "our reading": "That very state of things (the flattery the dohā describes) had come about for Rāvaṇa.", "alternatives": ["Rāvaṇa had found just such helpers (ministers who flatter out of fear or hope)"]}
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: A: that very state of things

issue: ममता अधिकाई: whose or what ममता grows is not stated — Rāvaṇa's show of affection for Mandodarī, or his sense of 'mine' (pride in his power and possessions).
our reading: He went to the assembly with his ममता (attachment) increased; kept neutral: बढ़ी हुई ममताके साथ / his attachment grown all the greater.
alternatives: showing her still greater affection (Gita Press: अधिक स्नेह दर्शाकर)
his pride / sense of possession swollen (attachment to self and kingdom)
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: B: showing her greater affection

issue: सोइ रावन कहुँ बनी सहाई: सहाई may be read as 'helpers' (the flattering ministers) or as 'help' meaning the situation or combination (fatal flattery) that the dohā just described.
our reading: Rāvaṇa had found just such helpers (ministers who flatter out of fear or hope).
alternatives: the same situation or combination had arisen for Rāvaṇa (Gita Press: वही सहायता (संयोग) आ बनी)
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: A: that very state of things

issue: कपि (singular in form) in 'जय कृपाल कहि कपि चले अंगद हनू समेत' may be Sugrīva, to whom Śrī Rāma has just said आनहु, going with Aṅgada and Hanumān, or the monkeys in general.
our reading: वानर / the monkeys set off with Aṅgada and Hanumān (Gita Press English likewise).
alternatives: Sugrīva (कपि = the monkey king) set off with Aṅgada and Hanumān (Gita Press Hindi: अंगद और हनुमान्‌सहित सुग्रीवजी).
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: B: Sugrīva, with Aṅgada and Hanumān

issue: 'हित अनहित मानहु रिपु प्रीता': हित/अनहित can be welfare/harm or well-wisher/enemy.
our reading: You take a well-wisher for a foe and an enemy for a friend (parallel with रिपु प्रीता, and fits Vibhīṣaṇa speaking of himself and Mālyavān).
alternatives: You take your good for harm and an enemy for a friend (Gita Press Hindi: हितको अहित).

review: Agree it is a genuine doubt. The entry should give the argument for the epithet reading: प्रतिपालक stands in a run of agent-noun epithets of the Lord ending in the rhyming घालक; Gita Press takes it of the words, as we do.
reviewer_fix: {"id": "sundar.50.cau2", "issue": "नीति प्रतिपालक: an epithet of the Lord (upholder of right counsel) or a description of his words (words that uphold right counsel)?", "our reading": "Of the words: 'नीतिकी रक्षा करनेवाले वचन' / 'words that upheld right counsel'.", "alternatives": "As one more epithet of the Lord, 'नीतिके पालक प्रभु' / 'the upholder of right counsel': प्रतिपालक is an agent noun like the other epithets in the list and rhymes with घालक."}
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: B: one more title of the Lord, upholder of right counsel

review: Missing doubt: we take बलरासि of Jāmbavān alone ('बलकी राशि जाम्बवान्'); Gita Press reads it of all the warriors named ('ये सभी बलकी राशि हैं'). The words allow both.
reviewer_fix: {"id": "sundar.54.do54", "issue": "बलरासि: an epithet of Jāmbavān only, or of the whole list?", "our reading": "Of Jāmbavān, the word next to it: 'बलकी राशि जाम्बवान्' / 'Jāmbavān, a mountain of strength'.", "alternatives": "Of all the warriors named: 'ये सब बलकी राशि हैं' / 'all of them mountains of strength' (Gita Press)."}
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: B: all of them mountains of strength

issue: निज स्वास समीर: whose breath fans the fire of Rāvaṇa's anger: Vibhīṣaṇa's (his own words of counsel, which provoked Rāvaṇa) or Rāvaṇa's own (snorting) breath?
our reading: Left as ambiguous as the verse: 'अपनी ही साँसकी प्रचंड हवा' / 'the fierce wind of his own breath'.
alternatives: Gita Press: Vibhīṣaṇa's breath, i.e. his words (स्वास = वचन). Others take निज as Rāvaṇa's own breath, the angry man's hot breathing. If the owner prefers one, name the person in the meaning.

issue: नीति प्रतिपालक: an epithet of the Lord (upholder of right counsel) or a description of his words (words that uphold right counsel)?
our reading: Of the words: 'नीतिकी रक्षा करनेवाले वचन' / 'words that upheld right counsel'.
alternatives: As one more epithet in the list of the Lord: 'नीतिके पालक प्रभु' / 'the upholder of right counsel'.
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: B: one more title of the Lord, upholder of right counsel

issue: सोषहिं … पूरहिं (and मिलवहिं in 55.cau4): Śuka reporting the monkeys' boasts in his own words (they will …), or quoting them directly (we will …)?
our reading: Reported in Śuka's words: 'वे सोख डालेंगे …' / 'They will dry up the ocean …'.
alternatives: Gita Press and its English give it as the monkeys' direct speech ('हम … सोख लेंगे' / 'We shall suck the ocean dry …').

issue: सकल चरित: the whole account in general, or the doings of the wicked men on the northern shore just slain (as Gita Press reads it).
our reading: सारी कथा / the whole story (left general, as the verse says).
alternatives: उन दुष्टोंका सारा चरित्र / all the doings of those wicked men
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: B: the doings of the wicked men just slain

issue: भूमि परा कर गहत अकासा: a direct taunt (he lies on the ground and grasps at the sky) or a simile for Lakṣmaṇa's boasting (like one lying on the ground trying to grasp the sky).
our reading: Direct: lying on the ground, he would grasp the sky with his hand; the younger ascetic's big talk.
alternatives: Simile: like one lying on the ground reaching for the sky, so is the younger ascetic's boasting
decided: owner, 2026-10-23: B: a simile
